# How do the Apollo cache and SaltLog logging affect request latency?

## How much does the Apollo cache reduce median request latency?

Enabling the Apollo cache reduced median request latency from 120 ms to 45 ms in every tested workload [F1]. A follow-up study confirmed that the Apollo cache cut median request latency roughly in half [F3]. In a replication across three services, the Apollo caching layer lowered median latency by about half [F4].

## How much overhead does SaltLog logging add per request?

Verbose SaltLog logging added roughly 3 ms of overhead to each request in the benchmark [F2]. In production traces, SaltLog added between 2 and 4 ms per request when verbose logging was on [F5].

## Sources

- [F1] Jane Doe (2024). Apollo cache halves median latency in read-heavy services. Journal of Invented Systems. https://doi.org/10.5555/apollo-a
- [F3] Kim Lee (2024). A follow-up on Apollo cache latency. Journal of Invented Systems. https://doi.org/10.5555/apollo-f
- [F4] Ravi Rowe (2024). Latency effects of the Apollo caching layer. Journal of Invented Systems. https://doi.org/10.5555/apollo-b
- [F2] Ada Byte (2024). SaltLog logging overhead per request. Journal of Invented Systems. https://doi.org/10.5555/saltlog-d
- [F5] Lin Quay (2024). Measuring SaltLog overhead in production. Journal of Invented Systems. https://doi.org/10.5555/saltlog-e

# How do the Apollo cache and SaltLog logging affect request latency?

## How much does the Apollo cache reduce median request latency?

Enabling the Apollo cache reduced median request latency from 120 ms to 45 ms in every tested workload [F1]. Turning on the Apollo cache brought median latency down from 120 ms to 50 ms on our staging cluster [F2]. A follow-up study confirmed that the Apollo cache cut median request latency roughly in half [F4]. In a replication across three services, the Apollo caching layer lowered median latency by about half [F5]. Our measurements show the Apollo cache cut median latency by roughly 60 percent for read-heavy endpoints [F6].

## How much overhead does SaltLog logging add per request?

Verbose SaltLog logging added roughly 3 ms of overhead to each request in the benchmark [F3]. In production traces, SaltLog added between 2 and 4 ms per request when verbose logging was on [F7]. Verbose SaltLog logging costs about 3 ms per request on our hosts [F8]. SaltLog adds 2 to 4 milliseconds per request when verbose mode is enabled [F9].

## Sources

- [F1] Jane Doe (2024). Apollo cache halves median latency in read-heavy services. Journal of Invented Systems. https://doi.org/10.5555/apollo-a
- [F2] Apollo cache latency guide. apollo-docs.example. https://apollo-docs.example/latency
- [F4] Kim Lee (2024). A follow-up on Apollo cache latency. Journal of Invented Systems. https://doi.org/10.5555/apollo-f
- [F5] Ravi Rowe (2024). Latency effects of the Apollo caching layer. Journal of Invented Systems. https://doi.org/10.5555/apollo-b
- [F6] Ops notes: Apollo in production. ops-notes.example. https://ops-notes.example/apollo
- [F3] Ada Byte (2024). SaltLog logging overhead per request. Journal of Invented Systems. https://doi.org/10.5555/saltlog-d
- [F7] Lin Quay (2024). Measuring SaltLog overhead in production. Journal of Invented Systems. https://doi.org/10.5555/saltlog-e
- [F8] What SaltLog costs. saltlog-blog.example. https://saltlog-blog.example/overhead
- [F9] SaltLog FAQ. saltlog-faq.example. https://saltlog-faq.example/faq
